title: Chapter 165: Who Is Playing Doctor?
html:
Mattresses littered the dark corridor, each bulging as though concealing something. Chen Ge tore one open with his hammer. Inside the rotting fabric lay a crude human figure assembled from pillows and sheets.

Most disturbing was the face painted across its pillow—eyes, a nose, and a gaping mouth rendered in childish strokes. The sight raised the hair on his arms.

“This makes no sense.” Resisting the urge to destroy it, Chen Ge considered the doll. “The Haunted House’s twenty-four mannequins are far more lifelike and frightening, yet they don’t bother me at all. This crude thing makes me profoundly uneasy.”

He nudged it and found an unfamiliar name written on the pillow’s reverse: Lee Chunyan.

“Why is there a name?”

The figures resembled dolls used in games of house, where children assigned each toy the role of a parent or someone they knew.

Chen Ge scattered salt across the painted face and watched for two minutes. Nothing happened. He moved to another mattress and opened it, revealing a second figure made from a pillow and bedsheets.

“Zhang Qisi?” Another name marked its back. He surveyed the mattress-filled corridor as a chill climbed his spine. “Does every doll bear a name? Are they meant to represent real people?”

The swollen mattresses resembled a mass grave, and sweat dampened his grip on the hammer. If he survived this Trial Mission, courage would never trouble him again. In only twenty or thirty meters, he emptied two packets of salt. It clearly had no effect; the oppressive unease filling the corridor had only intensified.

“I need to ration the last packet.” Every few steps, he looked over his shoulder, half-expecting the dolls to trail behind him like those in horror films.

His entire body taut, he decided that if one stood up, he would immediately smash it apart with the hammer and finish it with the cleaver.

“Calm down. You still have plenty of trump cards.” He did not know whether he spoke for the audience or himself. As he advanced, his viewership climbed at a frightening rate, while Qin Guang’s stream plateaued and began losing viewers.

Unlike the first two buildings, the Third Sick Hall consisted entirely of private rooms. Strangely, not one contained a bed; the place hardly seemed to have served as a hospital.

“Doctor Gao said the Third Sick Hall had ten rooms and nine recorded patients. What were all these other rooms for?”

Every identical white door lacked a number. None of the spaces beyond appeared designed to house patients.

“The first hall was so overcrowded that patients slept in the corridor, yet these rooms stood empty. Why would the hospital refuse to use them?”

He proceeded with extreme care. Halfway along the fourth-floor corridor, the stench abruptly thickened. Beneath the cold wind came another sound, difficult to identify—the labored breathing of a crowded room. Anxiety mounting, he swept the flashlight around, pressed his back to the wall, and checked his phone. “Midnight.”

At that instant, a door opened somewhere below. Though the sound came from another floor, it seemed to occur directly beside him.

The blood door in the Haunted House mirror appears for one minute at midnight. Does this hospital have a similar door?Such a door might materialize on its own, but it did not open without cause. If it had moved, something had emerged from behind it.

“Wang Haiming completed the final ritual in a bathroom. That proves there’s a large mirror in one of the hospital’s bathrooms.”

After midnight, the entire sick hall changed, like a sleeping monster opening its eyes. From the far end of the fourth floor, Chen Ge peered down the stairwell into absolute darkness. Anything might be waiting there, ready to spring from a hidden corner.

His eyelid twitched. Hammer ready, he stood at the top of the stairs and considered his options before switching off the flashlight. Psychiatric patients, lingering spirits, and creatures from behind the blood door all roamed the Third Sick Hall. Danger waited at every step.

A light would expose him and make him an easy target. He closed his eyes, opened them again, and waited for his vision to adjust before descending toward the third floor.

Though the mission remained unfinished, it had already produced one reward: his relationship with the white cat had improved. Once unwilling even to approach him, the cat had leaped onto his shoulder as soon as they entered the Third Sick Hall. Its claws dug through his clothes into the backpack, and it seemed determined never to release him.

“Don’t be afraid. Everything is still under control.” He stroked its head, and for once, it did not resist. Its mismatched eyes stared into the darkness.

The staircase seemed to stretch in the dark; descending one floor took two full minutes. Sealed windows made the third floor darker still, and he could barely distinguish the mattresses scattered along its corridor.

“The twisted-faced man vanished after entering. He didn’t leave a single footprint. Is he hiding in a room—or beneath a mattress, waiting to ambush me?”

Another nurses’ station occupied the third-floor corner. Curiously, its medicines and records stood in perfect order, and the spotless counter looked recently used.

Behind it, prescribed pills covered the work surface. Someone had sorted the colored tablets into white bags and labeled each with a patient’s name.

“Lee Chunyan? Zhang Qisi? Those names were written on the dolls upstairs. Does someone come here every night to dispense medicine to them?”

An absurd image formed in his mind: the Third Sick Hall as a child’s game, with dolls playing patients while someone acted as their doctor.

“Who would play something so depraved?” Studying the names on the counter, Chen Ge felt that he had overlooked something important.
